@@ -0,0 +1,96 @@
+---
+title: Microsoft Entra Agent ID default inactivity policy
+description: Configure the default Microsoft Entra Agent ID inactivity policy to disable inactive agent identities automatically
+author: jawoods
+ms.author: jawoods
+ms.topic: how-to
+ms.date: 10/13/2026
+ai-usage: ai-assisted
+
+#customer intent: As an identity or security administrator, I want to configure the default agent identity inactivity policy so that I can disable inactive agent identities.
+---
+
+# Microsoft Entra Agent ID default inactivity policy (preview)
+
+To ensure the security and manageability of agent identities for Microsoft customers, Microsoft Entra Agent ID provides a default inactivity policy to all tenants. This policy identifies inactive agent identities, notifies relevant users, and then proceeds to disable the identity if no new activity is detected. Organizations can use this default policy to clean up inactive agent identities regardless of their licensing status.
+
+The Agent ID default inactivity policy allows only limited customization. Customers who want to create custom lifecycle policies using additional policy rules and customization should ensure they have the appropriate license. More details here: [Agent lifecycle policies](/entra/id-governance/agent-lifecycle-policies.md)
+
+> [!IMPORTANT]
+> Agent ID lifecycle policies are in preview. Preview features are provided without a service-level agreement and aren't recommended for production workloads. Certain features might not be supported or might have limited capabilities.
+
+## Prerequisites
+
+### License requirements
+
+No license is required to use the Agent ID default inactivity policy.
+
+### Roles
+
+One of the following roles:
+
+- [Lifecycle Workflows Administrator](../identity/role-based-access-control/permissions-reference.md#lifecycle-workflows-administrator)
+- [AI Administrator](../identity/role-based-access-control/permissions-reference.md#ai-administrator)
+- [Agent ID Administrator](../identity/role-based-access-control/permissions-reference.md#agent-id-administrator)
+
+## Enable the Agent ID default inactivity policy
+
+Enable the default inactivity policy to notify owners and sponsors of inactive agent identities, then disable and delete the identities if the agents remain inactive.
+
+1. Sign in to the [Microsoft Entra admin center](https://entra.microsoft.com) using one of the supported roles listed above.
+1. Browse to **ID Governance** > **Lifecycle Workflows** > **Lifecycle Policies** > **Agent ID (Preview)**.
+1. Select **Default Agent Identity Inactivity Lifecycle Policy**.
+1. Select the **Policy Configuration** tab.
+1. Toggle **Enable policy**.
+1. Review the configuration, and then select **Save**.
+
+Once the policy is enabled, Microsoft Entra Agent ID periodically evaluates the agent identities within its scope. When an agent identity has been inactive for 60 days, the identity enters the notification and enforcement process.
+
+## Microsoft Entra Agent ID default policy behavior
+
+Agent identities that are inactive and subject to the default inactivity policy will move through the following stages. The actions and timeframes are not customizable for default policy users.
+
+| Days inactive | Action |
+| -- | -- |
+| 60 days | Notify the agent identity's sponsors and owners |
+| 90 days | Disable the agent identity |
+| 455 days | Delete the agent identity |
+
+To return an agent to an active state, a user should interact with the agent or otherwise cause it to take action. Users cannot freely retain inactive agents that are subject to the inactivity policy without making them active.
+
+Once an agent has been disabled or deleted, it can only be recovered by an owner or administrator. Sponsors are not authorized to reenable or restore agent identities.
+
+## Configure the Agent ID default inactivity policy
+
+Administrators can configure the default inactivity policy's scope and set fallback notification recipients.
+
+### Policy scope
+
+The default inactivity policy supports two scopes: **All Agent IDs** and **All Agent IDs except selected**. 
+
+- **All Agent IDs**: All agent identities are subject to the policy.
+- **All Agent IDs except selected**: The admin can choose specific identities to exclude from the policy. These identities can remain inactive indefinitely. 
+
+Use the **All Agent IDs except selected** option if your organization needs to ensure that seasonal agents, limited-use agents, or other agents that aren't usually active won't be disabled. 
+
+To exclude specific agent identities from the policy, choose **All Agent IDs except selected**. Then, choose **+ Select Agent IDs**, select the needed agent identities in the list that appears, and then choose **Select**. Select **Save** to save the changes to the policy.
+
+### Fallback notification recipients
+
+Notifications inform accountable representatives when an agent identity has been inactive for at least 60 days. When sponsors or owners are available for the agent identity, they will be notified. If no sponsor or owner is present, the system will notify any fallback recipients provided by the administrator.
+
+To provide a fallback recipient, enter one or more email addresses separated by spaces, commas, or semicolons and then select **Save**. Note that group mailboxes are supported.
+
+## Policy priority
+
+Customers with appropriate licenses can create multiple agent identity lifecycle policies with different scopes, rules, and actions. Policy priority determines which policy applies when an agent identity is included in more than one policy. 
+
+The default inactivity policy is always the last policy applied. Any active custom policies take precedence.
+
+To learn more, see [Microsoft Entra Agent ID lifecycle policies](agent-lifecycle-policies.md).
+
+## Related content
+
+- [Governing Agent Identities](agent-id-governance-overview.md)
+- [Microsoft Entra Agent ID lifecycle policies](agent-lifecycle-policies.md)
+- [Manage agents in the end-user experience](/entra/agent-id/manage-agent-identities-end-user.md)

englishSummary.headline: Agent ID default inactivity policy is documented
englishSummary.summary: The documentation describes a preview policy that notifies owners after 60 days of inactivity, disables identities after 90 days, and deletes them after 455 days. Administrators can enable it, configure its scope, and set fallback notification recipients.
englishSummary.adminImpact: Admins can use the policy without a license, but should exclude seasonal or limited-use agents if they must remain inactive.

 description: Learn how to automatically provision and deprovision user accounts from Microsoft Entra ID to Puzzel.
 ms.topic: how-to
-ms.date: 08/10/2026
+ms.date: 10/22/2026
+ai-usage: ai-assisted
 
 # Customer intent: As an IT administrator, I want to learn how to automatically provision and deprovision user accounts from Microsoft Entra ID to Puzzel so that I can streamline the user management process and ensure that users have the appropriate access to Puzzel.
 --- 
@@ -12,6 +13,15 @@ ms.date: 08/10/2026
 This article describes the steps you need to perform in both Puzzel and Microsoft Entra ID to configure automatic user provisioning. When configured, Microsoft Entra ID automatically provisions and deprovisions users to [Puzzel](https://www.puzzel.com/) using the Microsoft Entra provisioning service. For important details on what this service does, how it works, and frequently asked questions, see [Automate user provisioning and deprovisioning to SaaS applications with Microsoft Entra ID](~/identity/app-provisioning/user-provisioning.md). 
 
 
+> [!IMPORTANT]
+> To improve the security posture of application provisioning, Microsoft is retiring the **OAuth 2.0 Authorization Code Grant** for this application.
+>
+> **Migrate** affected provisioning jobs to **OAuth 2.0 Client Credentials Grant by March 31, 2027**, to avoid disruption to provisioning. After this date, provisioning jobs that continue to use Authorization Code Grant might stop working and could eventually be removed from the service.
+>
+> **This change doesn't affect SSO.** Existing provisioned users can continue signing in, but new users won't be provisioned and changes to existing users and groups won't be synchronized while provisioning isn't functioning.
+>
+> Follow [Configure Puzzel for automatic user provisioning with Microsoft Entra ID](puzzel-provisioning-tutorial.md#configure-automatic-user-provisioning-for-puzzel-in-microsoft-entra-id) in this article to migrate to OAuth 2.0 Client Credentials Grant.
+
 ## Supported capabilities
 > [!div class="checklist"]
 > * Create users in Puzzel.
modifiedFiles.commitMessage: • Added the Important retirement callout before “Supported capabilities,” including the March 31, 2027 deadline and configuration link. • Updated the date and AI metadata; preserved the rest of the article.

englishSummary.adminImpact: Migrate affected provisioning jobs by March 31, 2027, using the documented configuration steps. SSO is unaffected.

messageCenterItems.title: Microsoft Entra: Prepare for Microsoft to disable unused or unsuccessful SMS first-factor sign-in
messageCenterItems.summary: Microsoft will disable SMS first-factor sign-in in Microsoft Entra tenants with no successful or only unsuccessful SMS sign-ins in the past 30 days, starting mid-September to November 2026. SMS for MFA and password reset remains unaffected. Admins should review usage, notify users, and ensure alternate sign-in methods.
messageCenterItems.body:
Updated October 28, 2026: We have updated the timeline. Thank you for your patience. 

What and why

You are receiving this message because SMS first-factor sign-in is enabled in your Microsoft Entra tenant.

Microsoft has observed significant fraud activity targeting SMS first-factor sign-in. SMS is a phishing-susceptible authentication method, and leaving this capability enabled can create risk even when users are not actively or successfully using it.

SMS first-factor sign-in allows users, such as frontline workers, to sign in using only a registered phone number and a one-time passcode (OTP) sent by SMS, without entering a username or password.

SMS first-factor sign-in does not enforce multifactor authentication (MFA).

To help protect customers, users, and Microsoft services, Microsoft will automatically disable SMS first-factor sign-in in tenants that meet either of the following conditions:

  • No successful SMS first-factor sign-in activity has occurred during the previous 30 days.
  • All SMS first-factor sign-in attempts during the previous 30 days were unsuccessful.

This change affects only SMS as a first-factor sign-in method. Users can continue to receive SMS verification codes for multifactor authentication (MFA) and Self-Service Password Reset (SSPR).

We strongly recommend that you review this setting and recent SMS first-factor sign-in activity before rollout begins. If your organization still requires SMS first-factor sign-in, confirm that legitimate users can sign in successfully and ensure that they have another sign-in method registered.

Rollout schedule

  • Worldwide: Beginning in mid-September 2026 and expected to complete by end of November 2026 (previously late September)

During rollout, Microsoft will evaluate eligible tenants and disable SMS first-factor sign-in when the criteria described above are met.

Impact on your organization

Who is affected

  • Organizations with SMS first-factor sign-in enabled in Microsoft Entra
  • Tenants with no SMS first-factor sign-in activity during the previous 30 days
  • Tenants where all SMS first-factor sign-in attempts during the previous 30 days were unsuccessful
  • Users who rely exclusively on SMS first-factor sign-in

Platforms and services

  • Microsoft Entra ID
  • SMS first-factor passwordless sign-in (SignInNoPassword)
  • Microsoft Entra authentication methods policies

What will happen

  • Microsoft will review recent SMS first-factor sign-in activity in eligible tenants.
  • If no successful SMS first-factor sign-in activity occurred during the previous 30 days, Microsoft will clear the Use for sign-in setting.
  • If all SMS first-factor sign-in attempts during the previous 30 days were unsuccessful, Microsoft will clear the Use for sign-in setting.
  • Clearing Use for sign-in disables SMS first-factor sign-in for the tenant.
  • Users will no longer be able to use SMS as their only authentication factor for sign-in.
  • Users who rely exclusively on SMS first-factor sign-in must register and use another sign-in method.
  • SMS verification codes for MFA and SSPR will continue to work.
  • Other authentication methods, including password-based sign-in, are not affected.

Action required and recommendations

Review your Microsoft Entra authentication methods policy to determine whether SMS first-factor sign-in is intentionally enabled and still required.

Before rollout begins, we recommend that you:

  • Review SMS first-factor sign-in activity from the previous 30 days.
  • Identify users who currently rely on SMS first-factor sign-in.
  • Investigate unsuccessful SMS first-factor sign-in attempts.
  • Ensure affected users have at least one alternate sign-in method registered.
  • Communicate this change to affected users before rollout.
  • Migrate users to passkeys or another phishing-resistant authentication method where possible.
  • Disable SMS first-factor sign-in yourself if your organization no longer requires it.

To review or disable SMS first-factor sign-in:

  • Sign in to the Microsoft Entra admin center with an account assigned at least the Authentication Policy Administrator role.
  • Go to Entra ID > Authentication methods > Policies.
  • Select SMS from the list of available authentication methods.
  • Locate Use for sign-in under SMS-based authentication.
  • Clear Use for sign-in to disable SMS first-factor sign-in.
  • Save the policy.

Clearing Use for sign-in stops SMS first-factor sign-in. It does not prevent users from using SMS for MFA or SSPR.

Learn more

  • Configure and enable users for SMS-based authentication using Microsoft Entra ID | Authentication | Microsoft Entra | Microsoft Learn

Compliance considerations

QuestionAnswer
Does this change include an admin control?Yes. Administrators can control SMS first-factor sign-in through Microsoft Entra authentication method policies. Administrators can review, enable, or disable the Use for sign-in setting for SMS-based authentication.
